children: U.S. critical-materials provider Elmet Group will buy a stake in a unit of Vietnam's Masan Group for about $125 million and secure more than eight years' supply of tungsten, in a bid to strengthen its supply chain of the key metal used in defense and other high-tech industries.

Elmet will acquire a 4.99% stake in Masan High-Tech Materials from a subsidiary of Masan Group, which will remain the tungsten processor's controlling shareholder with about 87.46% ownership, the Vietnamese conglomerate said Thursday. The deal implies an equity valuation of about $2.5 billion for Masan High-Tech.

Elmet and Masan High-Tech also entered into long-term agreements, committing to annual volumes of about 1,250 metric tons of tungsten material. The contracts are expected to generate around $1.5 billion in gross revenue for the Vietnamese company over the initial term at prevailing tungsten prices.

Masan High-Tech Materials operates the Nui Phao Mine--one of the world's largest tungsten deposits--alongside an integrated refining complex that converts concentrate into high-purity tungsten chemicals, according to Elmet.

Masan Group said the transaction is the first of what could be similar partnerships with major tungsten customers in other markets, and reflects growing collaboration across strategic materials supply chains.

"Rising demand from AI infrastructure, semiconductors, aerospace, energy, and advanced manufacturing increases the importance of secure, stable and reliable supplies of tungsten and other critical materials," it said.
Shares of Masan Group rose as much as 2.7% on Thursday.
Earlier this week, Elmet signed a long-term tungsten concentrate offtake agreement with Tungsten West covering production from the Hemerdon Mine in Devon, England.
